claims.quote: Lean imposes no upper bound on the representation of natural numbers other than physical constraints imposed by the available memory of the computer.

says.covers: integers kept exact past two to the 53rd

claims.quote: In Lean's kernel, the interpreter, and compiled code, closed natural numbers are represented as efficient arbitrary-precision integers.
Because they are part of the kernel, if these primitives did not correspond to their definitions as Lean functions, it could undermine soundness.

says.needs: arithmetic primitives that agree with their logical definitions
says.by: proof checking by a small kernel

claims.quote: In compiled code, sufficiently-small natural numbers are represented without pointer indirections

says.adopted: small integers unboxed, large ones as bignums

claims.quote: The natural numbers are an inductive type , so the induction tactic can be used to prove universally-quantified statements.

says.covers: proofs about arithmetic the solver cannot decide

claims.quote: Integers are arbitrary-precision, limited only by the capability of the hardware on which Lean is running

says.covers: integers kept exact past two to the 53rd

claims.quote: In all integer division conventions, division by 0 is defined to be 0

says.adopted: division by zero defined as zero

claims.quote: Rational numbers, implemented as a pair of integers num / den such that the denominator is positive and the numerator and denominator are coprime.

says.covers: fractions kept exact

claims.quote: This is a "smart constructor" that divides the numerator and denominator by the gcd to ensure that the resulting rational number is normalized
To enable reasoning about floating-point numbers, Lean exposes a logical model of Float that is used in proofs.

says.adopted: a logical model of floating point

claims.quote: Other operations, such as trigonometric functions, are represented as opaque functions in Lean's logic.
The logical model is extensively empirically tested against the floating-point operations on all supported platforms.

says.needs: trust that compiled code agrees with the logic
says.by: a logical model of floating point

claims.quote: As long as FFI code does not modify the floating-point environment, Lean's runtime floating-point primitives match the model's specification.

says.covers: proofs that hold of the code's own arithmetic
says.by: a logical model of floating point

claims.quote: Not all operations are defined; some are instead opaque functions whose behavior cannot be reasoned about in Lean's logic.

says.covers: proofs that hold of the code's own arithmetic

claims.quote: Additionally, terms that require reduction to become syntactically equal can be checked by the kernel when they use only operations that are modeled in Lean's logic
However, the native_decide tactic can invoke the underlying platform's floating-point primitives that are used by Lean for run-time programs

says.covers: proofs that hold of the code's own arithmetic

claims.quote: This requires trusting the Lean compiler, interpreter and the low-level implementations of built-in operators in addition to the kernel.

says.needs: trust that compiled code agrees with the logic

claims.quote: Computations that use floating-point numbers are very efficient; however, the nature of the way that they approximate the real numbers is complex, with many corner cases.

says.covers: arithmetic as fast as a double's

claims.quote: Differences between platforms are resolved by choosing specific representations (for example, all NaN values are replaced by a single canonical NaN when any operation requests a bit representation) and by modeling only the subset of floating-point operations that are implemented identically on all supported platforms.

says.needs: only operations every platform implements identically
says.by: a logical model of floating point

claims.quote: Lean's trusted kernel is a small, robust implementation of a type checker for the core type theory.

says.adopted: proof checking by a small kernel

claims.quote: The presence of explicit proof terms makes it feasible to implement independent proof checkers, increasing our confidence.

says.covers: a proof a small checker can recheck
says.by: proof checking by a small kernel

claims.quote: The compiler can compile partial functions that the kernel treats as opaque constants for the purposes of reasoning.

says.needs: a proof that the function ends

claims.quote: The fun_induction tactic is a convenience wrapper around the induction tactic to use the functional induction principle.

says.covers: proofs about functions that call themselves

claims.quote: decide attempts to prove the main goal (with target type p ) by synthesizing an instance of Decidable p and then reducing that instance to evaluate the truth value of p .
The target is not allowed to contain local variables or metavariables.

says.needs: a closed goal with no variables

claims.quote: native_decide is a synonym for decide + native .
can be used to create invalid proofs whenever the native evaluation of a term disagrees with the kernel's evaluation.

says.needs: trust that compiled code agrees with the logic

claims.quote: External checkers ( lean4checker , comparator ) cannot check such proofs, as they do not have access to the Lean compiler.

says.covers: a proof a small checker can recheck

claims.quote: In addition to the standard axioms, proofs by native evaluation introduce a dedicated axiom for each computation that is asserted by the compiled code.

says.adopted: an axiom recorded for each trusted computation

claims.quote: In particular, they do not require trust in the correctness of the code generator, unlike native_decide .

says.covers: a proof a small checker can recheck

claims.quote: The omega tactic, for resolving integer and natural linear arithmetic problems.

says.adopted: the omega test without dark and grey shadows

claims.quote: It is not yet a full decision procedure (no "dark" or "grey" shadows), but should be effective on many problems.

says.covers: a decision procedure for linear integer arithmetic
says.by: the omega test without dark and grey shadows

claims.quote: If we encounter x / k or x % k for literal integers k we introduce new auxiliary variables and the relevant inequalities.

says.needs: division and remainder only by literal numbers
says.by: the omega test without dark and grey shadows

claims.quote: This model-based search is complete for LIA .

says.covers: a decision procedure for linear integer arithmetic

claims.quote: grobner solves goals that can be phrased as polynomial equations (with further polynomial equations as hypotheses) over commutative (semi)rings, using the Grobner basis algorithm.

says.covers: polynomial identities decided exactly

claims.quote: When the inequalities are over a dense linear order, linarith is a decision procedure: it will prove False if and only if the inequalities are unsatisfiable.

says.covers: a decision procedure for linear real arithmetic

claims.quote: While there is some special handling for non-dense orders like Nat and Int , this tactic is not complete for these theories and will not prove every true goal.

says.covers: a decision procedure for linear integer arithmetic

claims.quote: linarith uses an untrusted oracle to search for a certificate of unsatisfiability.
Given a list of such coefficients, linarith verifies that ∑ kᵢtᵢ = 0 using a normalization tactic such as ring .

says.covers: a proof a small checker can recheck

claims.quote: An extension of linarith with some preprocessing to allow it to solve some nonlinear arithmetic problems.

says.covers: proofs about arithmetic the solver cannot decide
says.by: nonlinear preprocessing by products of hypotheses

claims.quote: the assumption 0 R' (b1 - a1) * (b2 - a2) is added to the context (non-recursively)

says.defines: nonlinear preprocessing by products of hypotheses

claims.quote: A tactic for solving equations in commutative (semi)rings, where the exponents can also contain variables.

says.covers: polynomial identities decided exactly

claims.quote: The basic approach to prove equalities is to normalise both sides and check for equality.
coefficients (any rational number, embedded into the (semi)ring)
Note that 0 / 0 is generally defined to be 0 , so division cancelling out is not true in general.

says.covers: identities that cancel division

claims.quote: The linear_combination tactic attempts to prove an (in)equality goal by exhibiting it as a specified linear combination of (in)equality hypotheses, or other (in)equality proof terms

says.covers: proofs written by hand and checked by machine

claims.quote: The coefficients may be arbitrary expressions (with nonnegativity constraints in the case of inequalities).

says.covers: proofs about arithmetic the solver cannot decide

claims.quote: It proves the goal by generating an appropriate call to the tactic linear_combination .

says.covers: a proof a small checker can recheck

claims.quote: The polyrith tactic relied on an external Sage server which has been shut down.
